concepts.heading: Consent in the Digital Age
concepts.alt: A guide holding a phone with a heart and a tick on its screen
concepts.plain: Phones and apps changed how consent works between people.

concepts.heading: The Unique Challenges of Digital Consent
concepts.alt: A guide watching a photo float out of his phone and multiply into copies
concepts.plain: What you send can be saved, copied and passed on. It does not just go away.

concepts.heading: Foundational Principles
concepts.alt: A guide holding a phone that shows a loop arrow and a tick
concepts.plain: The same rules apply online: a yes is ongoing, specific and can be taken back.

concepts.heading: Practical First Steps
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting together with their phones face down, talking
concepts.plain: Start with a simple chat about what each of you is okay with online.

checks.after: The Unique Challenges of Digital Consent
checks.prompt: Why is digital consent different from in-person consent?
options: What you share can persist and spread
checks.explanation: What you share can persist and spread. Unlike physical consent, digital consent involves persistent artifacts.

checks.prompt: Someone shared a photo once. May you keep and share it forever?
options: Yes, once sent it is yours
checks.explanation: No, consent is ongoing. Consent is ongoing: Just because someone shared a photo once doesn't mean they consent to you keeping it forever or sharing it with others.

e6192f83-055a-4885-b753-d8d5e98ccfe6.takeaway: Consent applies online too. Ask first, and remember that what you send can last.

concepts.heading: Sexting, Nudes & Photo Sharing
concepts.plain: Sending sexy photos or messages is a normal thing many adults do.

concepts.heading: The Consent Framework for Intimate Content
concepts.alt: Each holding a phone, a speech bubble with a question mark and a tick between them
concepts.plain: Ask before you send. Agree on what happens to the photos afterwards.

concepts.heading: Legal Realities
concepts.alt: A guide holding a gavel and a phone with a padlock on its screen
concepts.plain: Sharing someone's private photos without their okay is against the law in most places.

concepts.heading: In Polyamorous Contexts
concepts.alt: Each holding a phone with a padlocked folder floating above it
concepts.plain: With more partners, be extra clear about who may see what.

checks.after: The Consent Framework for Intimate Content
checks.prompt: Before sending an intimate photo, what should be true?
options: The other person has clearly said they want it
checks.explanation: The other person has clearly said they want it. Before sharing, check that the other person has explicitly said they want to receive it.

checks.prompt: Sharing someone's intimate images without their consent is…
checks.explanation: Illegal in most US states. Non-consensual sharing of intimate images (NCII) — commonly called "revenge porn" — is illegal in the majority of US states and many countries worldwide.

5a7edd14-be07-44c1-9942-0f374faba23e.takeaway: Ask before sending or sharing private photos, and never pass on someone else's.

concepts.heading: Online Harassment & Stalking
concepts.plain: Online spaces should feel safe, but many people get harassed there.

concepts.heading: Forms of Digital Harassment
concepts.alt: A guide holding a phone flooded with angry red message bubbles, her other hand raised to block them
concepts.plain: It ranges from messages that will not stop to threats and tracking.

concepts.heading: Who Is Most at Risk?
concepts.plain: It happens to a lot of people, and some groups are targeted more.

concepts.heading: Supporting Others
concepts.alt: She comforts him with a hand on his shoulder while he holds his phone
concepts.plain: If it happens to someone you know, believe them and help them save the proof.

concepts.heading: Legal Protections
concepts.alt: A guide holding a shield with a gavel on it
concepts.plain: Many places now have laws against online stalking and harassment.

checks.prompt: Repeatedly messaging someone after they asked you to stop is…
checks.explanation: A form of digital harassment. Unwanted contact, such as repeated messages after being asked to stop, is a form of digital harassment.

checks.prompt: A friend is being harassed online. What is the first step the lesson lists?
options: Tell them to log off forever
checks.explanation: Believe them. If someone in your community is experiencing digital harassment: Believe them.

9181783f-1aed-45ed-bf13-34b833297426.takeaway: Online harassment is real harm. Save the proof, get support, and know the law may protect you.

concepts.heading: Digital Boundaries & Healthy Tech Habits
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting on a sofa comparing phones, a dotted line drawn between them
concepts.plain: Every relationship needs to talk about phones, social media and privacy.

concepts.heading: Common Digital Boundary Conversations
concepts.plain: Common topics: posting about each other, reply times and sharing location.

concepts.heading: The Autonomy Spectrum
concepts.alt: A guide pointing at a traffic light showing red, yellow and green
concepts.plain: Healthy means each person keeps their privacy. Demanding passwords is control.

concepts.heading: Navigating ENM Digitally
concepts.plain: With more partners, decide what goes online and who is shown.

concepts.heading: Creating Your Digital Relationship Agreement
concepts.alt: Two guides writing on a shared tablet together
concepts.plain: Sit down together and write out your own phone and online agreement.

concepts.heading: Digital Aftercare
concepts.alt: He sends a heart from his phone that lands as a warm blanket around her shoulders
concepts.plain: After a tense online moment, check in and care for each other.

concepts.heading: Building Positive Digital Habits
concepts.alt: A guide smiling at her phone as a small heart and a flower pop out of it
concepts.plain: Small kind messages build closeness.

checks.prompt: "You must share all passwords and let me check your phone anytime." Where does this sit on the autonomy spectrum?
checks.explanation: Controlling. The lesson places demanding every password and phone checks at the controlling end of the spectrum.

checks.prompt: Checking in after a difficult text conversation is an example of…
checks.explanation: Digital aftercare. Just as we practice aftercare in physical intimacy, digital interactions sometimes need aftercare too.

a1fbd0ec-727c-41a3-9472-3a2831a5c216.takeaway: Agree together on phone and online habits. Privacy is healthy, and demanding passwords is control.
